# Two Emissions Mechanisms in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the Acid Rain Program addressed sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector through distinct regulatory tracks. In the sulfur dioxide system, each covered allowance represented permission to emit one ton under an aggregate cap with trading.

Sulfur dioxide coverage expanded in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap, reached in 2010, was 8.95 million tons.

The nitrogen oxides component followed a different approach for certain coal-fired units. It began in 1996 and was rate-based, without a cap or allowance trading. The two pollutants therefore had distinct mechanisms and timelines.
